reasons.specificity: The inventory maps specific dollar figures, institutional names, and mechanisms (AUD 2 billion minerals financing, USD 258 million Lynas award, USD 886 billion defence budget, Hanwha 19.1% share rise, AUKUS Defense Investor Network 400 USD billion) to their named immediate sources within the single supplied article, distinguishing government statements, journalism, company releases, and scholarly antecedents rather than offering generic thematic summary.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly every major finding cell contains a verbatim or near-verbatim passage from the supplied article that accurately supports the claim-chain or transformation described; the few cases where interpretation is added (e.g. noting that two predicates are non-identical for F16, or that different instruments are assembled under one narrative for F6/F8) are warranted by the actual text rather than invented.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis surfaces non-obvious distinctions a casual reader would miss: that AUD amounts span grants, awards, loans, pledges, and program envelopes without a shared accounting basis; that the Hanwha procurement source and the share-price source address different predicates and cannot establish causation; that the nuclear-submarine rationale and White's cost-risk criticism are related but non-identical claims; and that multiple departmental citations may repeat the same official announcement rather than providing independent corroboration.
reasons.coherence: Attribution, scope statements, finding labels (F1–F16), table rows, and the dependence table are consistently aligned throughout; the inventory's stated limitation—that only the single supplied article was inspected and no cited original was independently checked—is maintained without contradiction across prose, tables, and scope assessments.
reasons.usefulness: The dependence table and claim-provenance inventory directly help a reader assess which dollar figures and mechanisms in the article rest on a single journalism intermediary, which rest on same-department administrative reporting, and which synthesise unlike instruments, providing a practical audit trail for follow-up verification even though only one source was supplied.
reasons.hallucination_risk: All quantitative claims attributed to the article (USD 258 million Lynas, AUD 840 million Arafura, 12%/37% semiconductor shares, KRW 151,000 Hanwha price, USD 886 billion defence budget, GBP 220 million NSSIF, AUD 4.1 billion GWEO, etc.) are verifiably present in the supplied text; the analysis does not invent consensus, fabricate contradictions, or assert that any number is absent when it appears; the one corrected finding (F3 chain label) is handled transparently without introducing unsupported claims.

score.one_line: A well-anchored, source-faithful claim-chain inventory that correctly traces specific numbers and mechanisms to named intermediaries, distinguishes instrument types and predicate differences, and maintains a consistent access-limitation caveat throughout.
